headline: Quantum computing used in 'first commercial game development' for C.L.A.Y. RPG
summary: MiTale Ltd. partnered with IBM Quantum Computing to develop C.L.A.Y. - The Last Redemption, utilizing an IBM simulator to generate game assets such as maps, characters, and graphics. This marks the first commercial game to use quantum computing techniques.
details: MiTale Ltd.'s narrative-driven post-apocalyptic RPG, C.L.A.Y. - The Last Redemption, is making headlines for its use of quantum computing techniques. Developed in collaboration with IBM Quantum Computing experts, the game leverages an IBM simulator to generate game assets like maps, characters, and graphic simulations.

This collaboration is touted as the "first commercial game on the market utilizing quantum computing in an immersive narrative experience." MiTale has been exploring quantum games since 2019, connecting quantum systems with familiar development environments including Unity, Unreal Engine, and Godot.

The studio has a longer-term goal of integrating real quantum hardware into game development. They hope this will enhance player-centered design and provide truly unique, real-time adjusting experiences in every gaming session.

MiTale also suggests that discrete or integrated quantum accelerators could one day "accelerate complex tasks in a manner similar to a GPU" within PCs. This hints at a future where quantum hardware becomes a new normal for complex tasks in gaming, much like NPUs in current systems.
